title: The configuration file .github/ci-config.yml, version 1
description: Switches shared parts of the pipeline on with their values and registers the repository's local workflows. A part runs when it is stated under parts; a part that is not stated is switched off. The smallest valid file is the line `version: 1`.

version.description: The schema version of this file. The pipeline reads the current version and the one before it.

parts.description: The shared parts that are switched on, each under its name with its values. A part without values is stated as `<part>: {}`.

additions.description: The additions workflow: after a failed pull-request run that reported recorded additions, commits them to the suite list on the pull request's branch, once per push, as the updater App. `suites` names the suite list. Invented example: {"suites": "ci/suites.json"}.

custom.description: The free job: runs a script of the repository after the setups that it names, on the GitHub-hosted runner that `runner-label` names or on ubuntu-26.04, with read permission only and without secrets, for CI that no other part covers. While the work waits for a shared part or for a setting of one, `request` and `waits-for` name the request and what it waits for, as a temporary entry of the local workflow register does, and repository hygiene reports when the part or the setting exists. Invented example: {"setups": ["python-3.14"], "script": "ci/check-licences.sh", "runner-label": "windows-2025", "request": 12, "waits-for": "python-licences"}.

runner-label.description: The label of the GitHub-hosted runner of the job. Without it, ubuntu-26.04. The script runs with Bash on every runner.

request.description: The number of the request issue in this repository for the shared part, or the setting of one, that takes over the work of the script. The schema accepts it alone; the register check of repository hygiene requires `waits-for` with it.

waits-for.description: What the work of the script waits for: the name of a shared part that does not exist yet, or `<part>.<setting>` for a setting that an existing shared part lacks. The schema accepts it alone; the register check of repository hygiene requires `request` with it. Once the part exists at v1, or knows the setting, repository hygiene reports it, as it does for a temporary entry of the local workflow register. Invented examples: "python-licences", "python-test.coverage".

dependabot-auto-merge.description: Dependabot auto-merge: merges a pull request of Dependabot whose updates are all patch or minor, and for GitHub Actions all from actions/*, once its required checks have passed. `suites` names the suite list, so that a commit of the updater App that changes only that file does not make the pull request manual. Invented example: {"suites": "ci/suites.json"}.

dotnet-test.description: The tests of one or more .NET test projects or solutions, each in a job of its own: dotnet build and then dotnet test, with the .NET SDK version the project names; a job fails when no test ran. A project that is a console test program states console-runner: its job runs dotnet build and then dotnet run, and the program's exit code is the result. Invented example: {"projects": [{"sdk-version": "10.0.x", "project": "tests/Shop.Tests/Shop.Tests.csproj"}, {"sdk-version": "10.0.x", "project": "tests/Shop.Checks/Shop.Checks.csproj", "console-runner": true}], "paths": ["src/", "tests/"]}.

projects.description: The test projects or solutions that are built and tested, one job per item; the smallest form is one item that names its sdk-version and its project.

sdk-version.description: The .NET SDK version that actions/setup-dotnet installs.

project.description: The test project or the solution that is built and tested, as a path relative to the repository root; with console-runner, the project of the console test program.

runner-label.description: The label of the GitHub-hosted runner of the item's job. Without it, ubuntu-26.04.

console-runner.description: The project is a console test program: a project without a test framework that exits with a non-zero code when a check fails. The job runs dotnet build and then dotnet run --project <project> --no-build in place of dotnet test, takes the program's exit code as the result and makes no check that a test ran. Without it, false.

full-recording.description: The full recording: records every entry file of the suite list every two weeks and proposes the changed stored lists as a pull request that merges itself once its required checks have passed. `suites` names the suite list and `validation-workflow` the workflow that runs the suites on a pull request. Invented example: {"suites": "ci/suites.json", "validation-workflow": ".github/workflows/validation.yml"}.

github-release.description: The release part: publishes a GitHub release with the named files for a pushed tag that matches a pattern of `tags` and carries a valid SSH signature of a key in the allowed-signers file on the default branch. The shared workflow release.yml runs it, which the fixed caller release.yml calls on a pushed tag; for any other tag, and without this part, that workflow publishes nothing and passes. Invented example: {"tags": ["v*"], "allowed-signers": ".github/allowed_signers", "files": ["dist/tool.zip"], "script": "ci/build-release.sh", "setups": ["dotnet-10"]}.

tags.description: The patterns of the tags that are released. `*` matches within one segment of a tag between `/`, `?` matches one character of a segment and `**` matches any number of segments; any other pattern matches that one tag. Invented example: ["v*"].

allowed-signers.description: The path, relative to the repository root, of the file with the SSH keys that may sign a release tag, in the format of ssh-keygen's allowed signers. It is read from the default branch, never from the tagged commit, so a tag cannot approve its own key. Invented example: ".github/allowed_signers".

files.description: The files that the release publishes, as paths relative to the repository root: files that `script` writes, or without `script` tracked files of the tagged commit. Each is published under its file name, so no two share a file name. Invented example: ["dist/tool.zip"].

title.description: The title of the release, in which `{tag}` stands for the tag and `{version}` for the tag without a leading `v`. Without it, the title is the tag. Invented example: "Tool {version}".

notes.description: The path, relative to the repository root, of a tracked file whose content becomes the release notes, the body of the release. It is read at the commit that the verified tag names, so it is a tracked file of that commit and never a file that `script` writes, and it holds UTF-8 text of at most 125000 characters. Without it, the body is the list of merged pull requests that GitHub generates for the tag since the previous release, the nearest earlier tag that matches a pattern of `tags` and has a published release, filtered by the part: it leaves out the titles of the types docs, style, refactor, test, build, ci and chore without `!` and the lines whose every author is a bot, and names only external contributors. Invented example: "docs/release-notes.md".

runner-label.description: The label of the GitHub-hosted runner of the job that runs `script`. Without it, ubuntu-26.04. It needs `script`, as `setups` does.

issue-title.description: Issue-title normalisation: gives an opened issue the title prefix of its category. `categories` names the repository's category file, a JSON object with the component categories under `product_categories` and the categories without components under `generic_forms`; both are lists, a missing one counts as empty, and together they hold at least one item. An item of `generic_forms` is an object with `key` (the name of the category, unique across both lists), `title_prefix` (the prefix that an issue of the category gets) and `labels` (the labels of which one on an issue makes it an issue of the category). An item of `product_categories` is an object with `key`, `title_prefix` and `labels` as well, and with `source_directory` (the folder, relative to the repository root, whose direct subfolders are the components), `marker` (the file in a component's folder that makes it a component; it starts with `key: value` lines between two `---` lines), `dynamic_title_prefix` (the prefix of an issue about a component, with `{component}` for the component's name), `component_label` (the heading of the component field in the issue form) and `required_metadata` (the keys that every marker must hold). Each value is a non-empty string, except `labels` and `required_metadata`, which are lists of non-empty strings and may be empty; every key is required, and a key that is not named here is ignored. Invented example of the setting: {"categories": "intake/categories.json"}. Invented example of the category file: {"product_categories": [{"key": "tool", "source_directory": "tools", "marker": "TOOL.md", "title_prefix": "[tool]", "dynamic_title_prefix": "[{component}]", "component_label": "Tool", "required_metadata": ["name"], "labels": ["category:tool"]}], "generic_forms": [{"key": "question", "title_prefix": "[question]", "labels": ["category:question"]}]}.

node-test.description: The install, build and tests of one or more Node projects with npm, each in a job of its own: the Node version of the project's .nvmrc, the npm version of packageManager in its package.json or else the npm of that Node, and then npm ci, npm run build when package.json defines the script build, and npm test. Invented example: {"projects": [{"working-directory": "web"}], "paths": ["web/"]}.

projects.description: The Node projects that are installed, built and tested, one job per project; the smallest form is one project that names its working-directory.

working-directory.description: The project's directory, relative to the repository root, that holds its package.json, its package-lock.json and its .nvmrc, and from which every npm command runs.

runner-label.description: The label of the GitHub-hosted runner of the project's job. Without it, ubuntu-26.04.

python-test.description: The Python tests of one or more projects, each project in a job of its own: pytest where the project configures it, otherwise unittest discover, on the Python version the project names; a job fails when the runner finds no tests. Invented example: {"projects": [{"python-version": "3.13", "working-directory": "backend", "install": "requirements-dev.txt"}], "paths": ["backend/"]}.

projects.description: The projects whose tests run, one job per project; the smallest form is one project that names its python-version.

python-version.description: The Python version, 3.11 or newer, that actions/setup-python installs as the job's own Python.

working-directory.description: The project's directory, relative to the repository root, from which the dependencies install and the tests run. Without it, the repository root.

install.description: What pip installs before the tests, pytest included where the project configures it: a requirements file ending in .txt (pip install -r) or an extra of the project (pip install ".[<extra>]"), both from working-directory. Without it, nothing is installed.

runner-label.description: The label of the GitHub-hosted runner of the project's job. Without it, ubuntu-26.04.

python-verify.description: The Python language checks of one or more projects, each project in a job of its own: ruff check, mypy where the project configures it, and optionally ruff format --check, on the Python version the project names. Invented example: {"projects": [{"python-version": "3.13", "working-directory": "backend", "install": "dev"}], "paths": ["backend/"]}.

projects.description: The projects that are checked, one job per project; the smallest form is one project that names its python-version.

python-version.description: The Python version, 3.11 or newer, that actions/setup-python installs as the job's own Python.

working-directory.description: The project's directory, relative to the repository root, from which the dependencies install and the checks run, and in which mypy's configuration is looked for. Without it, the repository root.

install.description: What pip installs before the checks, so that mypy sees the project's packages: a requirements file ending in .txt (pip install -r) or an extra of the project (pip install ".[<extra>]"), both from working-directory. Without it, nothing is installed.

format-check.description: Also run ruff format --check. Without it, false.

repository-hygiene.description: Repository hygiene: the convention checks, the credential scan and the shared checks that a change can affect. It always runs and cannot be switched off; stating it, as `repository-hygiene: {}` or with settings, only sets what its Dependabot coverage check and its link check leave out. Without the part or a setting, both checks read every file. Invented example: {"coverage-exclude": ["tests/fixtures/package.json"], "link-exclude": ["vendor/**/*.md"]}.

coverage-exclude.description: The package files that are test fixtures, which nothing installs, or folders of such files, each as a path relative to the repository root. The Dependabot coverage check leaves out a package file at or under a listed path, which then needs no entry under dependabot. A change to this setting starts the coverage check. Invented example: ["tests/fixtures/package.json", "tests/fixtures/node"].

link-exclude.description: Globs, relative to the repository root, of Markdown files whose links the repository does not maintain, such as vendored documentation: `*` matches within one path segment and `**` across segments, and a pattern that ends in `/` matches everything under that folder. The link check checks no link in a matching file and still checks a link from another file into one. A change to this setting starts the link check. Invented example: ["vendor/**/*.md", "third_party/"].

suite-selection.description: The suite selection: runs only the entry files of the suite list that a change can affect, each under the recording step, in Linux shards and one Windows job, and reuses the passed results of a pull request. `suites` names the suite list, which states the suites, the setups with one script each and the jobs' runner labels. `language-steps` names the language steps that the first Linux shard runs after its entry files. `pinned-tools` names the pinned tools, `node` and `gitleaks`: each is a setup of that name which the suite jobs give, on Linux and on Windows, at the version of the pins file of the revision of Shared Workflows that the run uses, Gitleaks after the sha256 check of its asset. A suite states a pinned tool under `setups`, or an entry file under `entry_setups`, as any other setup, and only the entry files that state it get it; the suite list defines no setup of that name, and none with `tool: node` beside `node`. The check of the configuration file fails on another name and on a name stated twice. The selection fails when the suite list defines a setup with the name of a pinned tool, when a setup states `tool: node` beside `node`, and, as for an undefined setup, when a suite states `node` or `gitleaks` that neither the suite list nor `pinned-tools` knows. A job fails before any entry file runs when the Gitleaks asset has another sha256 than the pins file states, and when the pins file holds no asset of the tool for the job's system. Invented example: {"suites": "ci/suites.json", "language-steps": ["python"], "pinned-tools": ["node", "gitleaks"]}.

language-steps.description: The language steps that the first Linux shard runs outside the recording when a change reaches their files.

pinned-tools.description: The pinned tools that the suite jobs give as setups at the version of the pins file, to the entry files that state them.

dependabot.description: The repository's Dependabot ecosystems, each under its name with the directories of its package files; a directory starts with `/`. `.github/dependabot.yml` is generated from it, one entry per ecosystem in this order; an ecosystem with several directories gets one entry that lists them, with one group that combines each update of a dependency across them into one pull request, and repository hygiene fails while the file differs. Without ecosystems the repository holds no Dependabot configuration. Invented example: {"github-actions": ["/"], "pip": ["/", "/tools/report"]}.

local-workflows.description: The register of the repository's workflows that are no fixed caller: one entry per workflow file.

paths.description: The part runs only when a changed path matches one of these patterns, when its own configuration changed, or when the changed files are unknown. A pattern is a path relative to the repository root with `/` separators: one that ends in `/` matches everything under that folder, `*` matches within one path segment, `?` matches one character of a segment, `**` matches any number of segments, and any other pattern matches that one path. Invented example: ["src/", "tests/**/*.py", "pyproject.toml"].

setup.description: The name of a setup that the pipeline knows: the tool and the version that a job installs before it runs code of the repository. The known setups are the names in setups.json beside this schema.

setups.description: The setups that a job installs, in the listed order, before it runs code of the repository; a later setup of the same tool is the one that its command names. An empty list installs nothing. Invented example: ["dotnet-10", "python-3.14"].

script.description: The path of a script of the repository, relative to the repository root, that a job runs with Bash from the repository root. Its exit status decides the job's result. A job that runs it has read permission only and receives no secret. Invented example: "ci/check-licences.sh".

file.description: The path of a file of the repository, relative to the repository root, with `/` separators. Invented example: "ci/suites.json".

oneOf.title: a temporary entry (workflow, request, waits-for)
oneOf.description: A workflow that stays local until the shared part it waits for exists, or until the part knows the setting it waits for. Invented example: {"workflow": ".github/workflows/nightly-report.yml", "request": 12, "waits-for": "python-release"}.

oneOf.title: a permanent entry (workflow, declined-request)
oneOf.description: A workflow that stays local because its request was declined. Invented example: {"workflow": ".github/workflows/weekly-monitor.yml", "declined-request": 15}.

declined-request.description: The number of the closed request issue in this repository that was declined.

request.description: The number of the request issue in this repository.

waits-for.description: What the work waits for: the name of a shared part that does not exist yet, or `<part>.<setting>` for a setting that an existing shared part lacks. Invented examples: "python-release", "python-test.coverage".

workflow.description: The path of the workflow file.

relative-path.description: A path relative to the repository root with `/` separators, without a `..` segment and without a leading `/` or `-`. Invented example: "services/api".

runner-label.description: The label of one GitHub-hosted runner, of the ubuntu-, windows- or macos- family, such as "windows-2025"; no other label, so that no job runs on a self-hosted runner.

dotnet-sdk-version.description: A .NET SDK version as a quoted string: one SDK ("10.0.403"), the newest patch of a feature band ("10.0.4xx"), of a minor version ("10.0.x") or of a major version ("10.x").

python-version.description: A Python version, 3.11 or newer, as a minor version ("3.13") or one patch of it ("3.13.2").

python-install.description: A requirements file ending in .txt, as a path relative to the project's directory, or the name of an extra of the project. Invented examples: "requirements-dev.txt", "dev".
